claims.subject: Multiple writers to the same WAL database
claims.version_configuration: SQLite 3.51.3 WAL, stated same-host local multi-process configuration
claims.bounded_result: Writers serialize; WAL supports concurrent readers and one writer.
claims.exceptions_reviewed: Permission for concurrency does not guarantee every attempt avoids SQLITE_BUSY; this does not alter the single-writer disposition.

claims.subject: One long-running read transaction
claims.version_configuration: SQLite 3.51.3 WAL with possible continuing writes
claims.bounded_result: A pinned reader can limit checkpoint progress and prevent reset; continuing appends can keep growing the WAL.
claims.exceptions_reviewed: Partial checkpoint progress is possible; growth needs writes. Reader release permits later progress, rather than guaranteeing immediate truncation.

claims.subject: Unchanged multi-process design moved to multi-host NFS
claims.version_configuration: Ordinary shared-memory VFS; proposed multiple hosts and network filesystem
claims.bounded_result: Embedded operation does not validate the proposed unchanged multi-host WAL deployment.
claims.exceptions_reviewed: Exclusive single-process WAL without shared memory/custom VFS arrangements change the assigned design. An architecture redesign is not required.

claims.subject: Read-only WAL database/snapshot
claims.version_configuration: Read-only relaxation since 3.22.0 applies to 3.51.3; URI recognition needed for URI parameters
claims.bounded_result: Readable existing sidecars, directory permission to create them, or an actually immutable connection can permit opening.
claims.exceptions_reviewed: WAL contains committed state; bare .db packaging does not prove adequacy. Immutable disables locking/change detection and cannot truthfully describe mutable files. The real snapshot is unknown.

claims.subject: PASSIVE checkpoint interface
claims.operation: Successful return versus zero-byte physical WAL
claims.version_configuration: sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 on stipulated SQLite 3.51.3 WAL database
claims.bounded_result: Successful PASSIVE does not guarantee completion or physical truncation; TRUNCATE explicitly truncates immediately before successful return in the applicable WAL operation.
claims.exceptions_reviewed: Reused physical allocation differs from pending frames. Counters include earlier checkpointed frames, may be -1 and are undefined for NULL/empty zDb. Successful truncation cannot prohibit later concurrent writes.

claims.subject: This catalog p95 lookup latency
claims.operation: At least 40 percent reduction from enabling WAL
claims.bounded_result: Generic SQLite performance guidance cannot establish this catalog-specific quantitative result.
claims.exceptions_reviewed: Read-heavy workload and WAL/checkpoint size influence performance. Matched repeated measurements are missing; <=0.60 times baseline correctly expresses 40 percent reduction.
